title: Config
description:
Root configuration for dfe-archiver.

Covers the archiver's own sections only. The memory guard, the metrics
listener and the scaling-pressure engine are scalo's, built by
`ServiceRuntime` before the archiver exists, and are configured through the
cascade (`DFE_ARCHIVER_MEMORY_*` for the guard, `--metrics-addr` /
`METRICS_ADDR` / `DFE_ARCHIVER_METRICS__ADDRESS` for the listener,
`DFE_ARCHIVER_SCALING__*` for the engine). A parallel `memory:` / `metrics:` /
`scaling:` block here parsed, validated and reached nothing.

## Hot-reload behavior

**Hot-reloaded**, because the pipeline re-reads it from the shared config:
- `kafka.batch_size` -- once per receive

**Requires pod restart** -- everything else. `Archiver` snapshots the config
at construction into `startup_config`, so a reload of `transport`,
`kafka.*`, `grpc.*`, `archive.*`, `buffer.*`, `routing.*`, `compression.*`
or `dlq.*` is accepted and validated but does not reach the running
pipeline. `restart_required_changes` names those sections, and
the reloader warns instead of reporting a reload.

transport.description:
Which transport carries records IN: `kafka` (a broker holds them between
stages) or `grpc` (the scalo Push listener, point to point). Same two
spellings as dfe-loader's `transport`, because a deployment sets both
from the one `kafka.mode` dial.

grpc.description: Push listener configuration, read when `transport` is `grpc`.

dlq.description:
Dead letter queue configuration. A field a `dlq:` block leaves out
keeps the archiver's default.

topics.description:
Topics to consume. Empty turns on scalo's broker-side auto-discovery,
filtered by `topic_include`/`topic_exclude` and refreshed every
`topic_refresh_secs`, so a source added after this pod started is
archived without a restart.

topic_include.description:
Regex patterns a discovered topic must match (OR). Empty means every
topic the broker holds that `topic_exclude` does not drop.

topic_exclude.description:
Regex patterns that drop a discovered topic (OR). Exclude wins over
include. Defaults to scalo's list, which already drops the DLQ and
Kafka's own internal topics.

topic_refresh_secs.description: How often the discovered topic list is re-read from the broker.

tls.description:
scalo's client TLS section, read with an `SSL` protocol. A private CA
is `trust: bundle` with `ca_paths`.

allow_insecure_transport.description:
Deliberately opt into an unencrypted transport (PLAINTEXT /
`SASL_PLAINTEXT`) in production. Defaults to false: scalo's
Kafka transport REJECTS plaintext in production unless this is set
(e.g. mesh-encrypted in-cluster traffic). Outside production it has no
effect.

acknowledgements.description:
With `enabled: true` (the default) a record's offset is committed only
once the archive file holding it is complete in the store, so a kill
re-reads what an open file held: duplicates are possible, loss is not.
With `enabled: false` offsets are committed as records are received,
and a kill loses what the open files and buffers held.

librdkafka_overrides.description:
Raw librdkafka properties for the consumer and the DLQ producer,
winning over every setting scalo derives. `message.max.bytes` here sets
the DLQ producer's record ceiling, and a dead letter over it is screened
out before the write. `statistics.interval.ms` stays 5000 unless this
map names it.

ClientTlsConfig.description:
The `tls:` section every TLS client reads: a profile, a trust choice, CA
files, an optional client certificate, key pins, the name the server's
certificate is checked against, and the key share sent first.

A transport that cannot honour a key says so at config load: Kafka takes no
pin, server name or key share, and `platform` trust only on Windows.

profile.description:
`strong` (default), `commercial` or `cnsa2`. Per-profile settings, such
as `allow_tls12`, live in the `tls.profiles` cascade section.

ca_paths.description:
CA PEM files, trusted beside the OS store under `native` and
`platform`, and alone under `bundle`. One path or a list.

client_cert_path.description: Client certificate PEM for mutual TLS, with `client_key_path`.

client_key_path.description:
Client private key PEM for mutual TLS, with `client_cert_path`. May
name the same file when it holds both.

pin_sha256.description:
SHA-256 pins on the server's public key, as in [`SpkiPin`]. Once the
chain verifies, the key must match one. Empty checks no key.

server_name.description:
The name checked against the server's certificate and sent as SNI.
Default the endpoint's host.

key_share.description:
`profile` (default) sends the profile's first group, a post-quantum
one. `classical` sends a classical share first.

CryptoProfile.description: A named TLS profile. `strong` is the default.

oneOf.description:
TLS 1.3 only unless the profile sets `allow_tls12`, AES-256-GCM,
ChaCha20 and AES-128-GCM, hybrid post-quantum key exchange first.

TLS 1.3 and 1.2, every ECDHE AEAD suite, hybrid post-quantum key
exchange first: the cheapest profile that is still current.

TLS 1.3 only, AES-256-GCM, ML-KEM-1024 then P-384, ECDSA P-384 and
ML-DSA-87 signatures. The CNSA 2.0 shape.

TrustChoice.description:
Which certificates a client accepts a server's certificate from.

Every choice trusts the CA files given beside it, and `bundle` trusts
nothing else.

oneOf.description:
The OS root store, read through `rustls-native-certs` and checked by
rustls.

The OS verifier, through `rustls-platform-verifier`, so Windows and
macOS apply their own policy and revocation checks.
Only the CA files given: an exclusive pin, with no OS root trusted.

SpkiPin.description: SHA-256 of a server certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, in base64 or 64 hex digits.

KeyShare.description: Which key share a client sends first.

oneOf.description: The profile's order: a post-quantum group first where it has one.

A classical group first, with the post-quantum groups listed but not
shared, for a receiver behind a middlebox that drops the larger
ClientHello. A server that prefers a post-quantum group asks for it in
a second round trip.

AcknowledgementsConfig.description:
The `acknowledgements` section of an ack-capable transport.

With `enabled: true` (the default) a source releases its acknowledgement --
a Kafka offset commit, a gRPC or HTTP response -- only once every piece of
work built from the record has been delivered, dead-lettered with the DLQ's
confirmation, or dropped by policy. A failed delivery withholds it, so the
record is delivered again: duplicates are possible, loss is not.

With `enabled: false` the source acknowledges at receipt, before the record
is processed: a crash or a failed delivery loses what was acknowledged.

```yaml
kafka:
  acknowledgements:
    enabled: true
```

enabled.description: Hold the source acknowledgement until every piece is delivered.

GrpcConfig.description:
Push listener configuration for the direct transport.

Mirrors dfe-loader's `grpc` block key for key, because both stages receive
the same scalo Push RPC and an operator reading one config should not have
to learn a second set of names.

listen.description: Listen address. Defaults to `0.0.0.0:6000`, the push port the deployment contract declares, so the Service and the listener agree.

recv_buffer_size.description: Records buffered from incoming RPCs before the sender is held.

acknowledgements.description:
The listener answers each push once its records are queued, with this
on or off: a record is released only when its archive file completes, at
the roll interval, long after any sender's deadline. So the archive copy
on this transport is at-most-once, and `enabled: false` only changes the
reason `pipeline_delivery_guarantee` reports, from `sink_cannot_confirm`
to `acks_disabled`.

destination.description:
Destination URL (file://, s3://, gs://, az://, minio://). Empty until an
operator names one, which is an idle archiver rather than a default
path: a container-local directory nobody asked for looks like it is
archiving and loses every file when the pod is replaced.

path_template.description:
Path template under the routed destination. The supported placeholders
are exactly {year}, {month}, {day}, {hour}, {minute}, {timestamp} and
{seq}; any other is refused at config validation, because the writer
would pass it through into the object key as literal braces.

roll_size_bytes.description: Rolling trigger: final compressed file size in bytes (not inbound data)

roll_interval_secs.description:
Rolling trigger: interval in seconds. Unset, it is 300 while the Kafka
consumer holds offsets (`transport: kafka` with
`kafka.acknowledgements.enabled`, the default) or on `transport: grpc`,
and 3600 otherwise. Every record in an open file keeps about 32 bytes
of held offset in memory until the file completes, and on `grpc` a kill
loses what the open files hold. A configured value always wins, and
one above 900 with offsets held logs a warning at startup.

multipart_chunk_size.description: Multipart upload chunk size in bytes (min 5MB for S3 compatibility)

max_writers.description:
Maximum number of archive writers open at once, one per routing
destination, evicted ones still closing included. At the cap the
least recently used writer is evicted and closed in the background,
and a write for a new destination waits for that close. Caps file
handles and bounds `dfe_archiver_unique_destinations` on
high-cardinality keys such as per-org routing.

S3Config.description: S3 configuration. A section with no `bucket` takes the destination URL's.

allow_http.description: Allow plaintext HTTP (for local/dev endpoints only). Defaults to false (HTTPS required).

GcsConfig.description: GCS configuration. A section with no `bucket` takes the destination URL's.

AzureConfig.description:
Azure Blob configuration. A section with no `container` takes the
destination URL's.

flush_bytes.description:
Flush a destination's in-memory buffer into its archive file once it
holds this many bytes, plus one record. A ceiling per destination: up
to 64 destinations buffer at once, and all of them together hold no
more than a quarter of the memory limit, past which the largest
buffers flush first.

flush_age_secs.description: Flush when buffer exceeds this age (seconds)

flush_records.description:
Flush a destination's in-memory buffer into its archive file once it
holds this many records, whatever its size.

writer_parallelism.description:
Object-store uploads of closed archive files running at once. Each
holds four parts of `archive.multipart_chunk_size` in memory. A local
destination has no uploads, so this does not apply to it.

spool_dir.description:
Directory holding `uploads/`, where object-store files are staged until
the store takes them, created at startup. Absolute because a relative
path resolves under the container WORKDIR, which appuser cannot write.

staged_bytes_cap.description:
Staged bytes past which intake pauses, and it must be above 0. Unset,
it is eight ninths of the spool budget, which is 90% of the size limit
the deployment declares for the volume under `spool_dir` (8 GiB on the
10Gi default). With no limit declared it is 8 GiB. Past the volume's
limit kubelet evicts the pod.

min_free_spool_bytes.description:
Free bytes the spool volume needs at startup when staging holds
nothing to upload. Unset, it is one ninth of the spool budget (1 GiB on
the 10Gi default), or 1 GiB with no declared limit.

quarantine_bytes_cap.description:
Bytes the quarantine directory under `uploads/` may hold before a file
sent there is removed instead. Unset, it is one ninth of the spool
budget (1 GiB on the 10Gi default), or 1 GiB with no declared limit.

expression_fields.description:
Field paths for expression-based routing (dot notation)
e.g., [`_org_id`, `tags.event_type`]. Unset, they are `[_org_id]` on
`transport: kafka` and `[_source, _org_id]` on `transport: grpc`.

default_segment.description:
Path segment for a field the record does not carry or carries blank, and
the destination of a record with no topic under `mode: topic`. `default`
is the deployment default org that `_org_id` takes when no sender set one.

codec.description:
Compression codec: none, zstd (`.zst`), lz4 (LZ4 frame format, `.lz4`),
snappy (snappy framing format, `.sz`), gzip (`.gz`). Each flush appends
one frame or gzip member.

queue_capacity.description:
Bounded mpsc capacity. When the queue is full, `try_send` returns
`QueueFull` (overflow=Drop). Sized for failure-burst tolerance.
Default 10_000.

batch_size.description:
Drain coalesces up to this many entries into one backend write.
Default 256.

flush_interval_ms.description:
Flush a partial batch after this duration, even if not full.
Default 100 ms.

max_payload_bytes.description:
Bytes an entry's payload and copied header values keep together: a
longer payload is cut and the entry marked `truncated` with its
original length, so it lands where the whole record could not, and a
header value that does not fit is left out. `None` keeps every
payload whole. Default [`DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`].

DlqMode.description: How backends are used when multiple are enabled.

oneOf.description:
Try backends in order. Stop on first success.
Default order: Kafka first, file fallback.

Write every batch to all enabled backends. The write succeeds when at
least one backend takes the whole batch, and fails only when none does.
Kafka backend only (matches a typical consumer's current behaviour).

FileDlqConfig.description:
File-based DLQ configuration.

Writes NDJSON files with automatic rotation and cleanup.

path.description:
Base directory for DLQ files.
Service name is appended as a subdirectory. Default `/var/spool/scalo/dlq`.

max_age_days.description: Auto-cleanup files older than this many days.

compress_rotated.description:
Codec for rotated files past the six newest: `none`, `gzip` or `zstd`.
Default gzip.

level.description: Level, by codec: gzip 1-9, zstd 1-22. Unset, the codec's default.

max_bytes.description:
Rotate before a write that would take the file past this many bytes.
A write into an empty file always lands, however large. Unset: no size
rotation. Works beside the time rotation: either rotates.

max_files.description:
Rotated files kept, newest first. Older ones are deleted at each
rotation. Unset: no count limit, only the age limit. Under `numbered`,
the highest number kept, and `0` deletes the file at each rotation.

naming.description: How rotated files are named: `stamped` (default) or `numbered`.

durable.description:
Sync the file's data to disk after each write, and its directory after
the file is created or rotated, so a write that returned `Ok` survives
power loss. Costs a disk flush per batch. Off by default.

file_mode.description:
Mode for files the writer creates, before the umask. Unset: `0666`
before the umask, except in the file transport, where it is `0600`.
Unix only: a Windows file takes its folder's ACL. Existing files keep
theirs.

dir_mode.description:
Mode for directories the writer creates, before the umask. Unset:
`0777` before the umask, except in the file transport, where it is
`0700`. Unix only.

RotationPeriod.description: File rotation period, by local time.

oneOf.description: Rotate before the first write in a new hour.
Rotate before the first write on a new day.
No time rotation. `max_bytes` can still rotate the file.

`<file>.1` newest to `<file>.<max_files>` oldest. Each rotation moves
every number up one. No compression and no age limit: their keys are
refused beside it.

FileMode.description: Unix permission mode in octal, such as "0600". Ignored on Windows.

topic_suffix.description: Suffix appended to destination for per-table routing.

common_topic.description:
Common topic when routing is `Common` or destination is unknown. Unset
by default, which names it after the service the DLQ is spawned for:
`<service>.dlq`, like the per-table `<destination>.dlq`, or `dlq` when
the service has no name. A value that is set is used as it is.

send_timeout_ms.description:
How long a `flush` or the shutdown waits for the broker to ack the
entries queued to Kafka, in milliseconds. Entries still unacked then
are purged and counted as dropped. The purge adds a wait of up to 5 s
for the purged entries' delivery reports, so `0` skips the ack wait
but not that one. Default 5000.

oneOf.description:
Route to topic matching destination with suffix.
e.g. "acme.auth" -> "acme.auth.dlq"
Route all failures to a single common topic.
